Writing lab note, Thursday.
Deepak came in again about his lab report, due Monday. He said he had been avoiding it since Tuesday and felt stuck at the very start. I did not tell him what to write. He said himself that he would type a single sentence in the blank document, nothing more, just to begin.
Sitting at the next desk, I watched him write a title sentence, then a second. Then he asked for water and went straight back. When I left an hour later he was still writing, with four paragraphs done. He told me starting was the hard part, not the writing.
I will check in on Saturday.
Zeenat, writing mentor

passage:
Monday

For five days I've avoided the lab report. Every evening I tell myself, "Tonight," and every evening I end up watching videos. Tushar, my roommate, asked if I'd started and I just groaned. Tonight I tried something he mentioned: tell yourself you'll do two minutes. Just open the document and type a single sentence. That's it, then you can stop. So at nine I opened the file. I wrote "The aim of this experiment was to measure the resistance of…" and then I needed to finish the sentence, so I did. Then I thought, might as well write the method. When I looked up, it was ten o'clock. Five paragraphs. It was the starting that was the monster, not the report. — Vishal
